```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(glue)
library(tsibbledata)
library(fpp3)
library(ggplot2)
library(broom)
data(PBS)
```

1\. Write a function to compute the mean and standard deviation of a time series, and apply it to the PBS data. Plot the series with the highest mean, and the series with the lowest standard deviation.

```{r}
#Get function and create mean and std dev variables for plotting
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  c(mean = mean(x, na.rm=TRUE), 
    sd=sd(x, na.rm=TRUE))
}

pbs_stats <- PBS |>
  features(Cost, mean_sd)
```

```{r}
#Filter highest mean value and lowest non-zero std deviation value and plot it
max_mean <- pbs_stats |>
  filter(mean == max(mean))

min_sd <- pbs_stats |>
  filter(sd > 0) |>
  filter(sd == min(sd))
```

```{r}
PBS |> 
  filter(Concession == max_mean$Concession, Type == max_mean$Type, ATC1 ==    max_mean$ATC1, ATC2 == max_mean$ATC2) |>
  
  autoplot(Cost) + 
    labs(title = "PBS series with the highest mean Cost")
```

```{r}
PBS |>
  semi_join(min_sd, by = c("Concession", "Type", "ATC1", "ATC2")) |>
  autoplot(Cost) +
  labs(title = "PBS series with the lowest std dev Cost")

```

2\. Use GGally::ggpairs() to look at the relationships between the STL-based features for the holiday series in the tourism data. Change seasonal_peak_year and seasonal_trough_year to factors, as shown in Figure 4.3.Which is the peak quarter for holidays in each state?

```{r}
data(tourism)
# View(tourism)

holiday_features <- tourism |> 
  filter(Purpose == "Holiday") |>
  features(Trips, feat_stl) |>
  mutate(
    seasonal_peak_year = factor(seasonal_peak_year),
    seasonal_trough_year = factor(seasonal_trough_year)
  ) 

holiday_features |>
  select(-Region, -Purpose) |>
  GGally::ggpairs(mapping=aes(colour=State))
  
holiday_features |>
  count(State, seasonal_peak_year) |>
  group_by(State) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1)  # keep the most common peak value in each state
```

3\. Use a feature-based approach to look for outlying series in the PBS data. What is unusual about the series you identify as “outliers”?

ropped

```{r}
pcs <- PBS_features |>
  select(-Concession, -Type, -ATC1, -ATC2) |>
  prcomp(scale = TRUE) |>
  augment(PBS_features)
pcs

pcs |>
  ggplot(aes(x = .fittedPC1, y= .fittedPC2, colour = Type)) + geom_point() + theme(aspect.ratio = 1)


outliers <- pcs |>
  filter(.fittedPC2 < -10) |>
  select(Concession, Type, ATC1, ATC2, .fittedPC1, .fittedPC2)
outliers
```

What is unusual is that all outliers have a very high PC1 value and that one of the outliers is a safety net which tends to cluster together more often.
